judgments.question: which file answers this question
judgments.sample_of: file finding questions, against a floor of 30 the recorded sessions could not reach
judgments.unanswerable_because: The one table that scored the two methods was struck on 2026-09-23 by bench/report/withdrawals.json, so there is no reading left to compare. 3 of the 4 questions name their own answer inside their own prompt, which makes that table a judge reading a filename out of the task against a BM25 with no stopword list, and nothing scored on it can be told apart from a regular expression pulling the filename out. The corpus is parked rather than rebuilt: the recorded sessions yield 7 recordable turns carrying 2 distinct tasks against a floor of 30, so there is nothing to rerun it on. What stands from the run is the cost and latency of Jev alone, 4 calls at $0.000063 a question and a p50 of about 333 ms, which says what the method costs and nothing about whether it wins.
judgments.unanswerable_evidence: Not yet decided, and it cannot be decided from four questions.
